thread:
Mira: uploaded a compact timeline mockup — thinking about how the canary pause/rollback affordances and the traffic handoff CTA surface in compact mode. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/compact-timeline (frame: compact-rollout-v3) Jonah: :eyes: looks tight. Quick thought — 'Pause canary' reads a bit like an internal term. Maybe 'Pause rollout' or 'Hold traffic' is clearer for non-engineer PMs? Priya: Prefer 'Pause rollout' — matches 'Resume rollout' elsewhere. Also flag: when compacted, rollback action gets hidden; worried operators won't find it fast. Sam: If rollback is buried in a kebab menu in compact mode, we need a persistent panic affordance (red) that surfaces instantly for SREs. Otherwise they'll miss it during incidents. Aisha: ran a quick contrast check on the current amber traffic pill — it fails WCAG AA on light bg (~3.1:1). Clickables need 4.5:1. Also keyboard order looks off in the prototype; focus should land on the primary action when the variant menu opens. Mira: noted. Proposed microcopy: primary CTA 'Pause rollout', secondary 'Rollback to previous', tertiary 'Open history'. Thoughts on length/clarity? Jonah: 'Rollback to previous' is explicit but a bit wordy. Maybe 'Rollback one version' — more explicit about scope. Priya: Users sometimes confuse 'rollback' with 'replay version' in docs. Can we add a tiny helper under the rollback action: 'Returns live traffic to a prior deployed version.' Short and clear. Sam: implementation note — need to announce state changes to screen readers. Example we propose: ```
Canary paused at 20% traffic
``` Aisha: aria-live=polite is fine for confirmations, but the panic/rollback should use role="alert" for immediate interruption. Also include visually-hidden text updates for toggles so NVDA/VoiceOver get explicit context. Mira: good call. We should also update the color tokens — will pick an amber/dark combo that meets 4.5:1 for interactive pills. Mira: layout question for the thread — should version history expand inline below the timeline (push content down) or open a right-hand drawer? Inline keeps context; drawer reduces layout thrash. Jonah: hybrid approach could work: show the latest 1–2 versions inline with a concise diff and a 'View all history' that opens a drawer for full commit metadata. Gives quick context without losing full detail. Priya: :thumbsup: hybrid is my vote. Inline items should show timestamp + author + a one-line commit snippet like 'fix: reduce kv-cache mem during warmup'. Sam: perf note — inline expansions must be lazy-loaded (no heavy diff/markdown parsing on initial page load). I'll estimate the extra payload and share in the implementation PR. Aisha: keyboard nav rule: when inline expands, move focus into the first interactive element inside the expansion. Provide a 'Back to timeline' skip link that restores focus. Also ensure the inline diffs are accessible to screen readers (heading levels, semantic lists). Mira: I'll update the frames in Figma with the copy changes, color tokens, and the hybrid history pattern. Will also add an accessibility layer (focus states & hidden helper text). Mira: @deploy-bot can you queue contrast + keyboard smoke tests once I push the branch feature/compact-timeline-aria? deploy-bot: Contrast and keyboard smoke tests queued for branch feature/compact-timeline-aria. Expected results in ~10m :hourglass_flowing_sand: Priya: thanks everyone — small follow-ups: 1) Mira, drop the new frames here when ready; 2) Sam, ping with perf estimate; 3) Aisha, can you list exact color token suggestions? Mira: will do. Thanks all!
